question: Who discovered the staining technique called 'Black reaction', which was capable of revealing neurons in their entirety?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Camillo Golgi**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Camillo Golgi** discovered the staining technique known as the 'Black reaction' in 1873.
 
• The 'Black reaction' or **Golgi's method** is a silver staining technique that allows for the visualization of neurons in their entirety, including their intricate structures.
 
• Golgi's method was a groundbreaking development in neuroscience, providing a way to study the detailed architecture of the nervous system.
 
• This technique was crucial in the advancement of neuroanatomy and contributed significantly to our understanding of the nervous system.
 
• Camillo Golgi was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1906** for his work on the structure of the nervous system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Camillo Golgi** was an Italian physician, pathologist, and scientist.
 
• His discovery of the Golgi apparatus, an essential cellular organelle, further cemented his legacy in the field of cell biology.
 
• The Golgi apparatus is involved in the modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins and lipids for secretion or use within the cell.
 
• Golgi's contributions laid the foundation for modern neurobiology and cellular biology, influencing numerous subsequent discoveries and advancements.
